target.title: fix(computer): reject malformed numeric input before node actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users invoking the `computer` tool through gateway-visible tool surfaces could provide malformed numeric values and have them coerced into desktop actions instead of rejected when issuing scroll, hold-key, or wait actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The computer tool now uses the existing strict numeric readers at the execution boundary for `scrollAmount` and `duration`, matching the owner-local guard pattern used by adjacent node-control numeric inputs. Valid defaults and the existing scroll clamp behavior stay intact; malformed present values fail before any node command or follow-up screenshot is invoked.

## User Impact

Malformed desktop-control numeric inputs now fail early with actionable validation errors, so invalid raw tool invocations cannot turn booleans, fractional scroll ticks, or nonnumeric durations into unintended computer-control actions.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: malformed computer numeric inputs are rejected before node invocation while valid scroll clamping remains unchanged.
- Current-head proof at `6c39afe6275c9378410dff43163d1d4efa92bfc1`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/computer-tool.test.ts` passed with 1 file and 65 tests passing.
- Branch diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Observed result: regression coverage rejects malformed `scrollAmount`, `hold_key` duration, and `wait` duration before invoking the node, and the existing oversized scroll clamp remains covered.
